text: Hello, I'm a newbie and wanted to know about launching a node. There are two types, which one is better? What server hardware do I need? What kind of internet connection do I need, and what's the approximate monthly income from a file node? Thank you.
Its a scam do not click!!!
@KikAss !node
!node
You could run in it on low spec hardware, even on a Pi5. Most important is bandwidth

There is currently one type - File Nodes used to serve download game data. You can choose to run your own pool or delegate to a public pool. If you decide to run your pool you will need a hardware that can be low as RaspberryPI or better, a good stable wired connection - the faster the better, and some knowledge about Docker, port forwarding and using Terminal commands. Rewards are on average somewhere 8-12 $RISE per node license/day, depending of your performance, global traffic, regional traffic and number of nodes active. If you decide to delegate, the pool operator you delegate to works for you, so you don't need anything above except for the node license and for return you are paying just the agreed fee, the rest is added to your account under rewards. (edited)

One BASE, one Cardano? Is there a difference? So, one license equals one node? If I buy one license, I can run one file node on a device. If I buy two licenses, I can run a second node on a different server, right?

They don't have any difference other than being on different chains. Both are completely the same utility vise. You can run up to 50 node licenses in one pool. If you have less than 6, you would have private pool, if you have more than 6 you can have public pool. The difference is that in public pool you are opening your pool for other to delegate to (for the poeple who have license but don't want to run their own pools). You can also run more than one full pool on your device if your bandwidth is good enough to handle the load (edited)
